chains.title: No TF-mediated effect of rs7001688
predictions: No allele-specific TF occupancy at this base in liver cells.
The only ChIP-supported TF, CTCF, is bound over the variant only in LNCAP, has no clear QBiC-SELEX allelic change, and has no HepG2 peak, so it does not support a liver allele-specific mechanism.
Any LDL-cholesterol association would be due to linkage disequilibrium with another causal variant, or rs7001688 would be a passenger variant.
falsified_if: Allele-specific TF occupancy, a reporter assay, or CRISPR base editing shows that this exact variant changes expression in liver cells.
Fine-mapping or functional assays show that rs7001688 itself, rather than a linked variant, is causal for LDL cholesterol.

chains.title: NME2 gains binding on the alt allele at a cryptic site and changes FAM110B expression
chains.element: The variant lies in an unannotated intronic/intergenic region with no overlapping cCRE and no cCRE within 500 bp; the nearest H3K4me3 cCRE is 1544 bp away. The QBiC-SELEX summary also notes that no occupied TF has a strong site at the variant, so a functional cryptic NME2 element is unproven.
chains.cell_type: Hepatocyte/liver-cancer line context (Hep 3B2.1-7; HepG2 as ENCODE liver-cancer stand-in)

links.claim: NME2 is predicted to bind the alt T allele more strongly in vitro: its own QBiC-SELEX model gives z=28.95, effect=0.573, and the alt site reaches the 99.1st percentile. NME2 is very highly expressed in Hep 3B2.1-7 (928.15 TPM, rank 1/1626 TFs). However, ENCODE has no NME2 ChIP peak in HepG2, and absence can also mean no NME2 experiment in that biosample, so occupancy at this variant is unknown.

The variant is not in an annotated cCRE and no cCRE is within 500 bp, so this would require an unannotated allele-specific NME2 binding element. The QBiC-SELEX summary adds that no occupied TF has a strong site at the variant, leaving the element speculative.

FAM110B is the nearest protein-coding gene at 420.6 kb, but there is no liver eQTL for the variant, no GWAS Catalog or Open Targets record for the variant, and no Open Targets association between FAM110B and free cholesterol in large LDL. E09 is only gene-level literature and does not establish variant-to-FAM110B regulation.
The liver/hepatocyte-like context is expression-compatible because NME2 is highly expressed in Hep 3B2.1-7, but NME2 occupancy at this variant is untested and no NME2 ChIP peak is reported in HepG2.

Allele-specific NME2 binding could alter FAM110B expression and LDL cholesterol, but this is inferential: there is no variant-level LDL cholesterol or statin-response evidence for rs7001688, and the FAM110B disease link is weak or absent in Open Targets.

predictions: Allele-specific NME2 ChIP or CUT&RUN in liver cells should show stronger T-allele occupancy at rs7001688.
A liver eQTL or allele-specific reporter should show that the T allele alters FAM110B expression if this chain is correct.
falsified_if: NME2 ChIP/CUT&RUN in liver cells shows no occupancy or no allele-specific binding at rs7001688.
Allele-specific reporter or CRISPR base editing shows no effect of the T allele on FAM110B expression or an LDL-related readout.
No eQTL, chromatin-loop, or perturbation evidence connects this variant to FAM110B.

chains.title: CASZ1 gains binding on the alt allele at a non-canonical site
chains.element: The variant is in an unannotated intronic/intergenic region with no overlapping cCRE and no cCRE within 500 bp, so a CASZ1-bound element here would be unannotated and unproven.

links.claim: CASZ1 is predicted to bind the alt T allele more strongly in vitro: its own QBiC-SELEX model gives z=32.75, effect=2.741, and the alt site reaches the 99.8th percentile. CASZ1 is only lowly expressed in Hep 3B2.1-7 (4.18 TPM, rank 776/1626), and ENCODE never assayed CASZ1, so occupancy is unknown.
No cCRE overlaps the variant and no cCRE is within 500 bp; the nearest H3K4me3 cCRE is 1544 bp away. This supports only an unannotated region, not a functional CASZ1 element.

FAM110B is the nearest protein-coding gene at 420.6 kb, but there is no liver eQTL for the variant and no variant-level GWAS/Open Targets record; Open Targets also shows no FAM110B association with free cholesterol in large LDL. Direct CASZ1-to-FAM110B regulation is not established.
CASZ1 expression is detectable in Hep 3B2.1-7, but at low level, so this chain requires a functional effect despite low TF abundance and unknown occupancy.

If the alt allele increases CASZ1 binding and CASZ1 regulates FAM110B, this could contribute to LDL cholesterol variation, but the direction and target gene are hypothetical and lack variant-level LDL evidence.

predictions: CASZ1 occupancy at rs7001688 should be detectable in liver cells despite low CASZ1 expression.
An alt-specific CASZ1 reporter or CRISPR edit should alter FAM110B expression if this chain is correct.
falsified_if: CASZ1 ChIP/CUT&RUN in liver cells shows no occupancy or no allele-specific binding at rs7001688.
Reporter or CRISPR base editing shows no T-allele effect in liver cells.
No eQTL or perturbation evidence connects the variant to FAM110B.

chains.title: TCF20 loses repressive binding on the alt allele and derepresses FAM110B
chains.element: The variant is not in an annotated cCRE and no cCRE is within 500 bp, so a functional TCF20 element here would be cryptic and unproven.

links.claim: TCF20 is predicted to bind the ref G allele slightly more strongly in vitro: its own QBiC-SELEX model gives z=-20.49, effect=-0.151, with the ref site at the 76.7th and alt at the 78.8th percentile. The site is weak on both alleles, QBiC-SELEX detects a change but the effect size is small, and TCF20 occupancy is unknown because ENCODE never assayed TCF20.
No cCRE overlaps the variant and no cCRE is within 500 bp, so this would require an unannotated TCF20 element; the evidence does not show that such an element is functional in liver cells.

If TCF20 represses FAM110B, loss of ref-allele TCF20 binding on the alt allele could increase FAM110B expression. However, FAM110B is 420.6 kb away, there is no liver eQTL for the variant, no variant-level GWAS/Open Targets record, and no Open Targets FAM110B association with free cholesterol in large LDL.
TCF20 is expressed in Hep 3B2.1-7 (23.44 TPM), making a liver-cell repressor mechanism expression-compatible, but occupancy and repressor function at this variant are untested.
Altered TCF20 repression of FAM110B could affect LDL cholesterol, but the direction and target gene are speculative and there is no variant-level LDL or statin-response evidence.

predictions: TCF20 ChIP or a reporter assay should show stronger G-allele binding and, if repressive, lower reporter activity.
The T allele should reduce TCF20 occupancy and increase FAM110B expression if this chain is correct.
falsified_if: TCF20 ChIP/CUT&RUN in liver cells shows no occupancy or no ref-allele preference at rs7001688.
A reporter or CRISPR edit shows no T-allele derepression of FAM110B.
No eQTL or perturbation evidence connects the variant to FAM110B.
